lesson.title: Check what it did
lesson.subtitle: Agents slip: check the call before it runs

video.title: Check what it did
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: Failed steps and a check in code

scenes.visual: A list: There’s no 9Z!; What did it do?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked an agent what class 9Z has tomorrow. There is no class 9Z in our school! It still looked something up and answered politely. So what did it actually do?

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how to check what an agent did, before you trust it.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: timetable{"class":"9C", …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here’s the call Darsi Tiny wrote. Look closely: the class says 9C, not 9Z. It has seen names like 9C far more often, so it copied the wrong one.

scenes.visual: A list: Copies words wrongly; “tidy” became “tisums”; New wordings: about 4 in 5 right; Never says it’s unsure.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Small models copy names and words wrongly. Once, “tidy” came out as “tisums”. New wordings trip them up too: about four in five right. And they never say they’re unsure.

scenes.visual: A list: Is it the right tool?; Every name from you or a result?; If not: stop it before it runs.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So, checking an agent means comparing its call with your request. Is it the right tool? Did every name and number come from your words, or from a tool’s result? If not, stop it before it runs.

scenes.visual: A list: The tool is switched on; Right shape: no 25:00; Names from you or a result; No earlier step failed; A person says yes to actions.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Our checker has five rules, written in code. The tool must be switched on. Details need the right shape, so twenty-five o’clock fails. Names must come from you or a result. No earlier step may have failed, and a person says yes to any action.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! You asked for a reminder to tidy the library. The call says “tisums the library”. What should happen?

scenes.visual: A list: Not in your words: stopped; Ask again, in other words; Strict rules never guess.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Stop it. That word isn’t in your request or in any result, so the checker stops the call. Then you ask again, in other words. The checker doesn’t need to be clever: strict rules never guess.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Checks matter for two-step jobs too. Ask for 6B’s first lesson on Saturday, with a reminder. The timetable says: no school. Darsi Tiny sets a reminder anyway, because it never checks a result before using it.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A rule like this takes only a few lines of Python. The program asks: is this detail in the request? If it isn’t, it stops and says why. You’ll fill in a check like this after the video.

scenes.visual: A list: Planner proposes, checker reviews; The weather request passes; 9Z → 9C: stopped; Checker off: try again.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: a planner and a checker
scenes.narration: In the app, Darsi Tiny plans and a checker of five rules reviews each call. Send the weather request: it passes. Then ask what 9Z has tomorrow, and watch the checker stop it. Turn the checker off, and try again.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Darsi Tiny wants to set a reminder for twenty-five o’clock. Which rule stops it?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Sure isn’t the same as right; Compare the call with your words; Rules in code stop slips.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Sure isn’t the same as right · Compare the call with your words · Rules in code stop slips
scenes.narration: The shape rule: there’s no twenty-five o’clock. Remember: an agent can be wrong and still sound sure. Check the call against your request. Simple rules in code stop slips before anything runs.

scenes.visual: A list: Look at what it did; Your words, exactly?; Write the slip and the rule.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: next time an app does something for you, look at what it actually did. Did it use your words exactly? Write down one slip you find, and the rule that would have caught it.

checkpoints.prompt: You asked for a reminder to tidy the library. The call says “tisums the library”. What should happen?

options.text: Stop it: that word isn’t in your request
Run it twice to be sure

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — every word in a call must come from your request or a tool’s result. “Tisums” comes from neither, so the checker stops it before it runs.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a slip in the call means a wrong reminder. Stop it, and ask again in other words.

checkpoints.prompt: Darsi Tiny wants to set a reminder for 25:00. Which rule stops it?

options.text: The tool must be switched on
Every detail needs the right shape
No earlier step may have failed

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a time runs from 00:00 to 23:59, so 25:00 doesn’t have the right shape, and the checker stops it.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the tool is on and nothing failed before. The time itself has the wrong shape: there is no 25:00.
